reason: The owner reported the iOS app broken on a real phone. An independent read found the lock screen dead on any physical device: the status line read the legacy BadgeReaderManager that nothing configures, the default keyboard-wedge provider listened for .badgeReaderKeyboardInput that nothing posted, Manual login was hidden unless managed config opted in, and DemoMode is compiled out on device. Underneath: BackendService fatalError'd on any http:// base URL ~30 s after launch (from the audit timer, even in demo mode), the session calls targeted /api/sessions/*, /api/badges/*, /api/auth/* and /api/audit/logs — none of which the served /v1 surface has — and OIDCAuthService force-unwrapped URLs built from <YOUR_TENANT_ID> placeholders. The cloud lane repaired all of this in the non-parity Swift files (DecisionEngine.swift / AppWorkflows.swift untouched) without a Swift toolchain. NOTHING here has compiled. This request is the build and the runs that prove or falsify it.
notes: ios-shell-repair (scripts/mac/ios-shell-repair.sh) IS the proof: one PASS/FAIL line per step — xcodegen generate; build for iPhone 17; demo launch (-DemoMode YES -SimulateBadge 04A3F291); no-flag launch with the local sign-in toggle OFF, asserting via the unified log (os_log subsystem com.enterprise.shell, row `lock_screen_presented … manual_login_available=…`) that NO row says true; toggle ON via `xcrun simctl spawn booted defaults write com.enterprise.shell local_session_allowed -bool true`, asserting a row says true (asam_probe must read `unavailable` on the simulator — if it reads notAttempted, the ASAM callback never fired and that is a finding); 40 s soak with -DemoBackendURL http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT:-8080} asserting alive AND no fatal/crash line (the api-server is probed first: GET /api/v1/context must answer 401 + JSON — start it with PORT=8080 pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run start; the server has no default port); accessibility-extra-large lock screen. Screenshots + logs land in artifacts/sim-results/ios-shell-repair-<date>/ — commit them with the result JSON. `--self-check` (no Xcode) was run by the cloud lane and passed; the real steps were not.

SETTINGS BUNDLE: open iOS Settings on the simulator and confirm an 'Enterprise Shell' entry appears with the group 'Unmanaged device' and the switch 'Allow local sign-in on this unmanaged device' (Settings.bundle/Root.plist + en.lproj/Root.strings). Expect compile errors in the build step: the cloud lane wrote ~1,300 lines of Swift with no toolchain. Fix syntax in place; if a fix would change behaviour, mail it back instead. Signing: project.yml no longer sets any signing value; the tracked native/ios/Signing.xcconfig carries the simulator defaults and `#include? "Signing.local.xcconfig"`. If xcodegen or xcodebuild complains about the include or about PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER (bundleIdPrefix was removed so the xcconfig governs), that is a finding — quote it.
